sentences.en: In 2011, the body of a woman was discovered in a California vineyard.
sentences.zh: 2011年，一名女性的遗体在加利福尼亚州的一个葡萄园中被发现。

sentences.en: She had been decapitated, and her body had been drained of blood.
sentences.zh: 她惨遭斩首，体内的血液已被排干。

sentences.en: It appeared her killer had gone to extraordinary lengths to conceal her identity.
sentences.zh: 凶手似乎费尽心机，试图掩盖她的身份。

sentences.en: For more than a decade, she was known only as Jane Doe.
sentences.zh: 十多年来，她一直被称为“无名氏”。

sentences.en: Then, detectives finally learned her name, Ada.
sentences.zh: 直到后来，侦探们终于查明了她的名字——艾达。

sentences.en: But, identifying her only made this bizarre murder even more perplexing.
sentences.zh: 然而，确认她的身份反而让这起离奇的谋杀案变得更加扑朔迷离。

sentences.en: Ada is the new series from Casefile Presents, available now wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 《艾达》是“案件档案呈现”系列的最新作品，现已在各大播客平台上线。

sentences.en: In the early hours of Sunday June 26, 2011, James Anderson, who went by his middle name of Craig, found himself in a predicament.
sentences.zh: 2011年6月26日星期日凌晨，詹姆斯·安德森（他习惯用中间名克雷格）陷入了困境。

sentences.en: He had locked his keys inside his car.
sentences.zh: 他把车钥匙锁在车里了。

sentences.en: It was a setback the happy-go-lucky 47-year-old African-American man wasn't prepared for.
sentences.zh: 对于这位47岁、性格随和的非裔美国人来说，这本是个他不该遇到的挫折。

sentences.en: Craig had gone out alone the previous evening as his husband of 18 years, James, was rostered on to work a night shift over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 前一天晚上，克雷格独自出门，因为他结婚18年的丈夫詹姆斯周末要上夜班。

sentences.en: Hours earlier, James had phoned Craig to remind him to start packing for their upcoming trip to Chicago in celebration of Craig's 48th birthday in five days' time.
sentences.zh: 几小时前，詹姆斯还打电话提醒克雷格开始收拾行李，准备五天后去芝加哥庆祝克雷格的48岁生日。

sentences.en: Their call ended with the men telling one another, I love you.
sentences.zh: 通话结束时，两人互道了“我爱你”。

sentences.en: Craig's orange Chevy Avalanche was parked in a lot off the Metro Inn, a budget hotel in his home city of Jackson, Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 克雷格的橙色雪佛兰Avalanche停在密西西比州杰克逊市的一家经济型酒店——地铁旅馆外的停车场里。

sentences.en: Located near the intersection of Highway 80 in the city's west, the lot was relatively small with around two dozen angled parking spots split into two near-even rows.
sentences.zh: 停车场位于该市西部80号公路的交叉口附近，规模较小，约有二十几个斜向停车位，分为两排，几乎对等。

sentences.en: A Wendy's fast food restaurant was located on its northern border, with winding on-and-off ramps for the Interstate 20 Highway to the south.
sentences.zh: 北侧是一家温蒂汉堡快餐店，南侧则是通往20号州际公路的蜿蜒匝道。

sentences.en: The lot was partially framed with small, tree-lined nature strips and could be accessed to the east, via Frontage Road, and to the west from the busy thoroughfare of Ellis Avenue.
sentences.zh: 停车场部分被绿树成荫的小型绿化带环绕，东侧可通过前置路进入，西侧则连接着繁忙的埃利斯大道。

sentences.en: Shortly after 4.45am, as Craig assessed his options, a white Jeep Cherokee SUV carrying four occupants entered the parking lot.
sentences.zh: 凌晨4点45分刚过，就在克雷格评估对策时，一辆载有四人的白色吉普切诺基SUV驶入了停车场。

sentences.en: Two young Caucasian men got out of the vehicle and approached Craig, who explained his dilemma.
sentences.zh: 两名年轻的白人男子下车走向克雷格，克雷格向他们说明了自己的困境。

sentences.en: He asked the pair if they had a coat hanger he could use to try and jimmy the lock in his car door.
sentences.zh: 他问这两人有没有衣架，想试着撬开车门锁。

sentences.en: The men moved back and forth between their Jeep and Craig's car, engaging Craig in conversation, while seemingly looking for an item that could be of assistance.
sentences.zh: 这两人在吉普车和克雷格的车之间来回走动，一边与克雷格交谈，一边似乎在寻找能帮忙的工具。

sentences.en: Fifteen minutes later, a dark green Ford F-250 pickup truck carrying three occupants drove into the car park, before leaving via the Ellis Avenue exit.
sentences.zh: 十五分钟后，一辆载有三人的深绿色福特F-250皮卡车驶入停车场，随后又从埃利斯大道的出口离开。

sentences.en: The two men who were helping Craig got back into their Jeep and followed the Ford.
sentences.zh: 那两名帮克雷格的男子回到吉普车上，跟在了福特皮卡后面。

sentences.en: Moments later, both vehicles returned and stopped in close vicinity to where Craig was waiting by his car.
sentences.zh: 片刻之后，两辆车都返回并停在了克雷格等待车辆的附近。

sentences.en: The two men who had assisted Craig earlier emerged from the Jeep and were joined by the driver of the Ford, a young, white, blonde-haired, blue-eyed male.
sentences.zh: 之前帮过克雷格的两名男子从吉普车上下来，福特车的司机也加入了他们——那是一个年轻、白皮肤、金发蓝眼的男子。

sentences.en: Suddenly, one of the men from the Jeep punched Craig in the face, knocking him to the ground.
sentences.zh: 突然，吉普车上的一名男子一拳打在克雷格脸上，将他击倒在地。

sentences.en: The driver of the Ford then straddled Craig and proceeded to hit him repeatedly around the head, while cussing and shouting racial abuse.
sentences.zh: 福特车司机随即跨坐在克雷格身上，对着他的头部反复猛击，同时口中咒骂着种族歧视的脏话。

sentences.en: The remaining passengers of the group's two vehicles watched on as the assailant spent the next three and a half minutes beating Craig.
sentences.zh: 两辆车上的其余乘客在一旁围观，行凶者花了整整三分半钟殴打克雷格。

sentences.en: Afterwards, he stole Craig's mobile phone, wallet, and wedding ring, before jumping back into the driver's seat of the Ford.
sentences.zh: 随后，他抢走了克雷格的手机、钱包和结婚戒指，然后跳回福特车的驾驶座。

sentences.en: As the Jeep drove away, one of its passengers yelled out,
sentences.zh: 当吉普车驶离时，其中一名乘客大喊道：

sentences.en: White Power!
sentences.zh: “白人至上！”

sentences.en: In response, the driver of the Ford raised his fist in the air and yelled back,
sentences.zh: 作为回应，福特车司机举起拳头，大声喊道：

sentences.en: White Power!
sentences.zh: “白人至上！”

sentences.en: As the Ford pulled out of the parking lot, its headlights illuminated Craig stumbling along the edge of Ellis Avenue, just to the right of the exit.
sentences.zh: 当福特车驶出停车场时，车灯照亮了正在埃利斯大道边缘蹒跚而行的克雷格，他就在出口右侧。

sentences.en: The driver steered towards him, mounted the curb, and ran him over.
sentences.zh: 司机径直朝他开去，冲上路缘，将他碾压在车下。

sentences.en: The Ford's occupants yelled more racial abuse out of the window, as the vehicle sped away.
sentences.zh: 福特车上的乘客从窗户里喊出更多的种族歧视辱骂，随后车辆加速逃离。

sentences.en: The state of Mississippi is located in America's deep south, bordered by Louisiana, Alabama, and Arkansas.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州位于美国深南部，与路易斯安那州、阿拉巴马州和阿肯色州接壤。

sentences.en: During the 1800s, black slaves were used to tend to the farming land that was owned by Mississippi's white citizens,
sentences.zh: 19世纪期间，黑人奴隶被用来照料密西西比州白人公民拥有的农田，

sentences.en: and by 1860, these slaves accounted for 55% of the state's population.
sentences.zh: 到1860年，这些奴隶占该州人口的55%。

sentences.en: The state was so heavily invested in slavery that race became a dominant theme of Mississippi's politics.
sentences.zh: 该州对奴隶制的投入如此之深，以至于种族问题成为了密西西比州政治的主导主题。

sentences.en: On January 9, 1861, Mississippi declared secession from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 1861年1月9日，密西西比州宣布脱离美国联邦，

sentences.en: Union and became one of America's original Confederate states.
sentences.zh: 成为美国最初的邦联州之一。

sentences.en: In the Declaration, slavery was referred to as, quote, the greatest material interest of the world.
sentences.zh: 在《独立宣言》中，奴隶制被称为“世界上最伟大的物质利益”。

sentences.en: In April that same year, the ongoing controversy between the southern and northern states over the enslavement of black people gave rise to the American Civil War.
sentences.zh: 同年4月，南方各州与北方各州之间关于奴隶制的持续争议引发了美国内战。

sentences.en: Over 80,000 Mississippians fought in the war, many of whom were motivated by fear of losing white supremacy.
sentences.zh: 超过8万名密西西比人参加了战争，其中许多人是出于对失去白人至上地位的恐惧。

sentences.en: During this time, the majority of Mississippi's black population were enslaved and living on plantations.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，密西西比州的大多数黑人人口都被奴役并生活在种植园里。

sentences.en: Many had been forced there by ship or over land via the domestic slave trade.
sentences.zh: 许多人是通过海路或陆路经由国内奴隶贸易被强行带到那里的。

sentences.en: In 1865, when the Confederacy was defeated and the Civil War ended, slavery was abolished by the 13th Amendment to the United States Constitution,
sentences.zh: 1865年，当邦联战败、内战结束时，美国宪法第13修正案废除了奴隶制，

sentences.en: with Mississippi being one of the few states that voted against the amendment.
sentences.zh: 而密西西比州是少数几个投票反对该修正案的州之一。

sentences.en: Five years later, Mississippi rejoined the U.S.
sentences.zh: 五年后，密西西比州重新加入了美国联邦，

sentences.en: Union, but the state continued to face intense interracial conflict and was centre stage during the civil rights movement of the mid-20th century.
sentences.zh: 但该州继续面临激烈的种族冲突，并在20世纪中期的民权运动中处于中心地位。

sentences.en: This was most evident in the state's capital city, Jackson.
sentences.zh: 这一点在州首府杰克逊市表现得最为明显。

sentences.en: Known as the City with Soul, Jackson is renowned for its music, architecture, museums, historic cultural districts, performing arts, and vibrant nightlife.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊被称为“灵魂之城”，以其音乐、建筑、博物馆、历史文化区、表演艺术和充满活力的夜生活而闻名。

sentences.en: However, like the rest of Mississippi, the city has a dark and complex history when it comes to racial inequality.
sentences.zh: 然而，和密西西比州的其他地方一样，这座城市在种族不平等问题上有着一段黑暗而复杂的历史。

sentences.en: Between 1877 and 1950,
22 people were lynched in Jackson's Hines County, more than anywhere else in the state.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊的海恩斯县有22人遭到私刑处死，比该州任何其他地方都多。

sentences.en: In 1954, the federal government's forced end to segregation resulted in Jackson becoming more racially diverse.
sentences.zh: 1954年，联邦政府强制结束种族隔离，导致杰克逊的种族多样性增加。

sentences.en: This prompted many white people to move away from the city, rendering some neighbourhoods of Jackson almost exclusively black.
sentences.zh: 这促使许多白人搬离该市，使杰克逊的一些社区几乎变成了纯黑人社区。

sentences.en: One of the most infamous hate crimes that occurred in Mississippi was the 1955 murder of 14-year-old Emmett Till, a black teenager who allegedly wolf-whistled at a white woman.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州发生的最臭名昭著的仇恨犯罪之一，是1955年14岁的黑人少年埃米特·蒂尔被谋杀案，他据称曾对一名白人女性吹口哨。

sentences.en: In retaliation for this perceived slight, two white men kidnapped and killed Emmett before dumping his body into the Tallahatchie River.
sentences.zh: 为了报复这种所谓的冒犯，两名白人男子绑架并杀害了埃米特，随后将他的尸体扔进了塔拉哈奇河。

sentences.en: An all-white jury acquitted the man, even though they later admitted to the murder.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些人后来承认了谋杀，但一个全白人陪审团还是判决他们无罪。

sentences.en: Another race-fuelled incident occurred in 1964, when two 19-year-old black men,
sentences.zh: 另一起种族仇恨事件发生在1964年，当时两名19岁的黑人青年，

sentences.en: Charles Moore and Henry D., were murdered by members of the white supremacist hate group the Ku Klux Klan in the Mississippi town of Roxy.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·摩尔和亨利·D，在密西西比州的罗克西镇被白人至上主义仇恨组织“三K党”成员杀害。

sentences.en: Charles and Henry were tied to a tree, beaten, and then dumped in the Mississippi River to drown.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯和亨利被绑在树上殴打，随后被扔进密西西比河溺死。

sentences.en: That same year, a gang of Ku Klux Klansmen that included several police officers abducted and murdered one black man,
sentences.zh: 同年，一个包括几名警察在内的三K党团伙绑架并谋杀了三名民权工作者：一名黑人男子，

sentences.en: James Cheney, and two white Jewish men,
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·切尼，以及两名白人犹太男子，

sentences.en: Andrew Goodman and Michael Schwerner, in Neshoba County, because they were trying to help black people register to vote.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·古德曼和迈克尔·施韦纳，地点在内肖巴县，因为他们试图帮助黑人登记投票。

sentences.en: During the 1960s, several serious crimes were committed against civil rights activists by white supremacists, and racist aggression was constant.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代，白人至上主义者对民权活动人士犯下了多起严重罪行，种族主义侵略行为层出不穷。

sentences.en: In 1963, civil rights activist Medgar Evers was shot outside his home by a member of the Ku Klux Klan, which caused national outrage
sentences.zh: 1963年，民权活动家梅德加·埃弗斯在家门外被一名三K党成员枪杀，这引起了全国范围的愤怒，

sentences.en: and was pivotal to the passing of the Civil Rights Act the following year.
sentences.zh: 并对次年《民权法案》的通过起到了关键作用。

sentences.en: From 1980 to 1990,
Jackson's white population dropped to 43%, and by 2000, white people accounted for just over a quarter of the city's population.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊的白人人口降至43%，到2000年，白人仅占该市人口的四分之一多一点。

sentences.en: Although that number showed a slight increase by 2011, racially motivated crimes committed by white people against the city's black citizens remained prevalent.
sentences.zh: 尽管到2011年这一数字略有上升，但白人针对该市黑人公民的种族动机犯罪依然普遍。

sentences.en: Craig Anderson had lived in Jackson, Mississippi for most of his adult life.
sentences.zh: 克雷格·安德森在密西西比州的杰克逊市度过了他成年后的大部分时光。

sentences.en: He was originally from Holmes County and was primarily raised by his mother after his father died.
sentences.zh: 他来自霍姆斯县，父亲去世后主要由母亲抚养长大。

sentences.en: Craig was one of four children, with an older sister and two younger brothers.
sentences.zh: 克雷格有四个兄弟姐妹，上面有一个姐姐，下面有两个弟弟。

sentences.en: He grew up to become a kind and courteous person who was particularly caring towards children and the elderly.
sentences.zh: 他长大后成为一个善良且有礼貌的人，尤其关爱儿童和老人。

sentences.en: His defining feature was what his sister Barbara called his grand piano smile.
sentences.zh: 他最显著的特征是他姐姐芭芭拉所说的“大钢琴式微笑”。

sentences.en: As a young man,
sentences.zh: 年轻时，

sentences.en: Craig moved 70 miles south to Jackson, where in 1993, at the age of 30, he was introduced to James, another African-American man.
sentences.zh: 克雷格搬到了南边70英里外的杰克逊，1993年，30岁的他结识了另一位非裔美国人詹姆斯。

sentences.en: James later told journalist Albert Samaha from BuzzFeed News that by the end of their first date, the pair had fallen for one another.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯后来告诉BuzzFeed新闻的记者阿尔伯特·萨马哈，在第一次约会结束时，两人就已经坠入爱河。

sentences.en: The cautious and organised James kept Craig in check, while Craig's warm and easygoing personality allowed a James to loosen up a little.
sentences.zh: 谨慎而有条理的詹姆斯约束着克雷格，而克雷格温暖随和的性格让詹姆斯能够放松一些。

sentences.en: On a number of occasions,
sentences.zh: 在多次旅行中，

sentences.en: James surprised Craig with trips to cities like Chicago,
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯曾给克雷格惊喜，带他去芝加哥、

sentences.en: New Orleans, and Miami.
sentences.zh: 新奥尔良和迈阿密等地旅游。

sentences.en: There, the couple were more comfortable being affectionate in public, unlike in Jackson, where members of the LGBTQI community often faced discrimination.
sentences.zh: 在那里，这对情侣在公共场合表现得更加自在，不像在杰克逊，LGBTQI群体经常面临歧视。

sentences.en: Five years into their relationship,
sentences.zh: 交往五年后，

sentences.en: James and Craig bought a house in Jackson.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯和克雷格在杰克逊买了一栋房子。

sentences.en: James wasn't initially keen on the property as he thought it was ugly, but Craig saw its potential and spent the next few years turning it into a home.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯起初并不喜欢这处房产，觉得它很丑，但克雷格看到了它的潜力，花了几年时间把它变成了一个家。

sentences.en: He put in new flooring, painted the walls, renovated the kitchen, and planted a garden full of flowers.
sentences.zh: 他铺了新地板，粉刷了墙壁，翻新了厨房，还种了一个开满鲜花的花园。

sentences.en: Craig also picked out all of the furniture and decorated the house with plush green carpet and paintings of tigers.
sentences.zh: 克雷格还挑选了所有的家具，并用毛绒绒的绿色地毯和老虎画装饰了房子。

sentences.en: The couple were active churchgoers at the First Hyde Park Missionary Baptist Church, where Craig sang as tenor in the choir.
sentences.zh: 这对情侣是第一海德公园传教士浸信会的活跃成员，克雷格在唱诗班担任男高音。

sentences.en: Craig and James had been together for 11 years and knew they wanted to spend the rest of their lives together.
sentences.zh: 克雷格和詹姆斯已经在一起11年了，他们知道自己想共度余生。

sentences.en: At the time,
sentences.zh: 当时，

sentences.en: Mississippi didn't recognise same-sex marriage, so they held a private ceremony in New Orleans, where they exchanged vows and rings.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州不承认同性婚姻，所以他们在新奥尔良举行了私人仪式，交换了誓言和戒指。

sentences.en: Months later,
sentences.zh: 几个月后，

sentences.en: Craig was offered a job as a production technician at a Nissan vehicle manufacturing plant in Canton, roughly 20 miles north of Jackson.
sentences.zh: 克雷格在坎顿的一家日产汽车制造厂获得了一份生产技术员的工作，那里位于杰克逊以北约20英里处。

sentences.en: Craig was thrilled as the position was higher paid than his previous job, and James later told BuzzFeed News that he'd reacted by, quote, jumping around, smiling like it was
sentences.zh: 克雷格非常激动，因为这份工作的薪水比他之前的工作高，詹姆斯后来告诉BuzzFeed新闻，克雷格当时的反应是“又蹦又跳，笑得像这是

sentences.en: the best day of his life.
sentences.zh: 他一生中最美好的一天”。

sentences.en: The couple celebrated with a trip to Memphis, Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 这对情侣去田纳西州的孟菲斯旅行庆祝了一番。

sentences.en: In 2007, a situation arose within James' extended family that resulted in a relative needing to re-home their newborn baby boy.
sentences.zh: 2007年，詹姆斯的大家庭中出现了一个情况，一位亲戚需要为刚出生的男婴寻找领养家庭。

sentences.en: James was eager to adopt, but Craig wasn't sure they were ready for the responsibility.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯渴望领养，但克雷格不确定他们是否准备好承担这份责任。

sentences.en: They decided to proceed with the adoption, and Craig immediately embraced the role of a devoted father.
sentences.zh: 他们决定继续领养，克雷格立刻承担起了慈父的角色。

sentences.en: He loved spoiling their adopted son with chocolates and toys.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢用巧克力和玩具宠爱他们领养的儿子。

sentences.en: James later stated,

sentences.zh: 约翰·赖斯和迪伦·巴特勒都被指控犯有一项共谋罪和一项违反2009年《联邦仇恨犯罪预防法》的仇恨犯罪罪。

sentences.en: These charges were in relation to their history of racially motivated crime, including the murder of Craig Anderson.
sentences.zh: 这些指控与他们有种族动机的犯罪历史有关，包括谋杀克雷格·安德森。

sentences.en: All three young men denied being racist or being raised to have a hatred of African Americans.
sentences.zh: 这三名年轻人均否认自己是种族主义者，也否认从小就被灌输对非裔美国人的仇恨。

sentences.en: Regardless, the next day of March 22, 2012, they each pleaded guilty, marking the first time that the Hate Crimes Prevention Act had ever been used
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，在次日2012年3月22日，他们每人都认罪了，这标志着《仇恨犯罪预防法》首次被用于

sentences.en: in a case where the defendant's actions resulted in a victim's death.
sentences.zh: 被告行为导致受害者死亡的案件中。

sentences.en: They appeared in court for sentencing in February 2015, three years and seven months after Craig Anderson's murder.
sentences.zh: 他们在2015年2月出庭接受判决，距离克雷格·安德森遇害已经过去了三年零七个月。

sentences.en: Judge Carlton Reeves, the second black federal judge in Mississippi's history, presided.
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿·里夫斯（Carlton Reeves）法官，密西西比州历史上第二位黑人联邦法官，主持了庭审。

sentences.en: James prepared a statement to be read on his behalf during proceedings, as he still couldn't bear to speak publicly about his husband's murder.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯准备了一份声明，要求在诉讼过程中代为宣读，因为他仍然无法忍受公开谈论他丈夫的谋杀案。

sentences.en: It read,
sentences.zh: 声明写道：

sentences.en: You all don't have a clue what you have really done to my family in committing this terrible crime.
sentences.zh: “你们根本不知道犯下这起可怕罪行对我的家庭造成了什么。”

sentences.en: James Craig Anderson was a great man.
sentences.zh: “詹姆斯·克雷格·安德森是一个伟大的人。”

sentences.en: He was a man who loved his family and was a great provider to our son and me.
sentences.zh: “他是一个爱家的人，也是我和我们儿子的坚强后盾。”

sentences.en: We had a great life and we miss him so much.
sentences.zh: “我们曾拥有美好的生活，我们非常想念他。”

sentences.en: Since his death, our lives have been turned upside down.
sentences.zh: “自从他去世后，我们的生活天翻地覆。”

sentences.en: James spoke of the detrimental impact
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯谈到了

sentences.en: Craig's murder had on his own mental health, his inability to work, and the challenges he had since faced as a single parent.
sentences.zh: 克雷格遇害对他自身心理健康造成的损害、他无法工作的情况，以及他作为单亲家长所面临的挑战。

sentences.en: Quote,
sentences.zh: 他说：

sentences.en: My heart gets so heavy at times because I feel like a failure because I couldn't keep up the things Craig did for us.
sentences.zh: “我的心有时感到非常沉重，因为我觉得自己是个失败者，因为我无法维持克雷格为我们所做的一切。”

sentences.en: We were always there for each other.
sentences.zh: “我们总是互相支持。”

sentences.en: We supported each other and we confided in each other.
sentences.zh: “我们互相扶持，互诉衷肠。”

sentences.en: I wish none of you would ever see daylight again.
sentences.zh: “我希望你们永远不要再见到天日。”

sentences.en: There is no room on earth for people like you.
sentences.zh: “地球上没有你们这种人的容身之地。”

sentences.en: Judge Carlton Reeves delivered a long and powerful sentencing speech that touched on the state's troubled past with lynchings and racial injustice.
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿·里夫斯法官发表了一篇漫长而有力的判决词，触及了该州在私刑和种族不公正方面的沉重历史。

sentences.en: Quote, On June 26, 2011, four days short of his 49th birthday, the blood of James Craig Anderson was added to Mississippi's soil.
sentences.zh: 他说：“2011年6月26日，在詹姆斯·克雷格·安德森49岁生日的前四天，他的鲜血洒在了密西西比的土地上。”

sentences.en: New generations have attempted to pull Mississippi from the abyss of moral depravity in which it once so proudly floundered in.
sentences.zh: “新一代人试图将密西西比从它曾经引以为傲的道德堕落深渊中拉出来。”

sentences.en: Despite much progress and the efforts of the new generations, these three defendants are before me today.
sentences.zh: “尽管取得了很大进步，且新一代人做出了努力，但这三名被告今天还是站在了我的面前。”

sentences.en: They and their co-conspirators ripped off the scab of the healing scars of Mississippi, causing her to bleed again.
sentences.zh: “他们和他们的同谋者撕开了密西西比正在愈合的伤疤，使她再次流血。”

sentences.en: There is absolutely no doubt that in the view of the court, the victims were targeted because of their race.
sentences.zh: “毫无疑问，在法庭看来，受害者是因为他们的种族而成为目标的。”

sentences.en: The simple fact is that what turned these children into criminal defendants was their joint decision to act on racial hatred.
sentences.zh: “简单的事实是，让这些孩子变成刑事被告的，是他们共同决定根据种族仇恨行事。”

sentences.en: In the eyes of these defendants and their co-conspirators, the victims were doomed at birth.
sentences.zh: “在这些被告及其同谋者眼中，受害者从出生起就注定要遭殃。”

sentences.en: Their genetic makeup made them targets.
sentences.zh: “他们的基因构成使他们成为了目标。”

sentences.en: On top of the two life sentences
sentences.zh: 在两项终身监禁的基础上，

sentences.en: Daryl Dedman had received for the state capital murder charge,
sentences.zh: 达里尔·德德曼因州谋杀罪被判处，

sentences.en: Judge Reeves sentenced him to an additional
sentences.zh: 里夫斯法官又判处他额外

sentences.en: 50 years in prison for his federal hate crimes.
sentences.zh: 50年监禁，罪名是联邦仇恨犯罪。

sentences.en: Dedman would first serve his 50-year sentence in a federal prison and then be moved to a state facility to serve out his two life sentences.
sentences.zh: 德德曼将首先在联邦监狱服完50年刑期，然后被转移到州立监狱服完他的两项终身监禁。

sentences.en: John Rice, who had instigated the unprovoked attack on Craig, was given 18 years and four months imprisonment.
sentences.zh: 约翰·赖斯，他煽动了对克雷格的无端袭击，被判处18年零4个月监禁。

sentences.en: Dylan Butler, who was present but didn't participate, was sentenced to seven years.
sentences.zh: 迪伦·巴特勒，他在场但未参与，被判处7年监禁。

sentences.zh: 司法部长

sentences.en: cast a broad net to ensure that all who commit such acts are brought to justice.

sentences.zh: 乔纳森·加斯坎普（Jonathan Gascamp）参与了高尔夫球场的袭击并发出死亡威胁，他还被控一项共谋罪和一项仇恨犯罪罪。

sentences.en: He was sentenced to four years.
sentences.zh: 他被判处四年监禁。

sentences.en: He was one of three people charged for their participation in the racist gang but who was not present for Craig Anderson's murder.
sentences.zh: 他是因参与该种族主义团伙而被起诉的三人之一，但他并未在克雷格·安德森（Craig Anderson）遇害现场。

sentences.en: Another who was not present for Craig's murder,
sentences.zh: 另一位未在克雷格遇害现场的人，

sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·多米尼克（Joseph Dominic）达成了一项协议，放弃大陪审团起诉，作为交换，他承认了一项共谋实施仇恨犯罪的罪名。

sentences.en: He was sentenced to four years.
sentences.zh: 他被判处四年监禁。

sentences.en: Judge Carlton Reeves acknowledged the court's belief that if it wasn't for Craig Anderson's death, the youths would have returned to Jackson to continue their mission to harm.
sentences.zh: 卡尔顿·里夫斯（Carlton Reeves）法官认可了法庭的观点，即如果不是因为克雷格·安德森的死亡，这些年轻人本会回到杰克逊继续他们的伤害任务。

sentences.en: The remaining members of the racist gang,
sentences.zh: 该种族主义团伙的其余成员，

sentences.en: John Blalack,
sentences.zh: 约翰·布拉拉克（John Blalack），

sentences.en: Shelby Richards and Sarah Graves were each charged with committing a hate crime against Craig Anderson which carried a possible life sentence.
sentences.zh: 谢尔比·理查兹（Shelby Richards）和莎拉·格雷夫斯（Sarah Graves）每人都被控对克雷格·安德森实施仇恨犯罪，可能面临终身监禁。

sentences.en: They, along with the John Rice, were also charged with willfully conspiring to cause bodily harm to African Americans in Jackson.
sentences.zh: 他们和约翰·赖斯（John Rice）一起，还被控蓄意共谋在杰克逊对非裔美国人造成人身伤害。

sentences.en: Blalack and Robert Rice also received charges for the attacks leading up to Craig's murder, including for carrying a firearm.
sentences.zh: 布拉拉克和罗伯特·赖斯（Robert Rice）还因导致克雷格遇害前的袭击事件而受到指控，包括携带枪支罪。

sentences.en: Shelby Richards and Sarah Graves faced additional charges for enlisting others to commit hate crimes and in the case of Graves, for lying to the FBI to conceal the fact
sentences.zh: 谢尔比·理查兹和莎拉·格雷夫斯还面临额外指控，罪名是招募他人实施仇恨犯罪；格雷夫斯还因向联邦调查局撒谎以掩盖事实而受到指控，

sentences.en: that the crime was racially motivated.
sentences.zh: 即该犯罪是出于种族动机。

sentences.en: Blalack,
sentences.zh: 布拉拉克、

sentences.en: Robert Rice,
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·赖斯、

sentences.en: Richards and Graves cited drunken judgement, youthful foolishness and peer pressure from Daryl Dedman for their participation in the attacks.
sentences.zh: 理查兹和格雷夫斯将他们参与袭击的原因归咎于醉酒判断失误、年少无知以及受达里尔·德德曼（Daryl Dedman）的同伴压力影响。

sentences.en: They each pleaded not guilty and were released on a $100,000 unsecured bond pending trial.
sentences.zh: 他们每人都拒不认罪，并在候审期间以10万美元的无担保保释金获释。

sentences.en: However, several months later, all four changed their pleas to guilty.
sentences.zh: 然而，几个月后，四人都改口认罪。

sentences.en: Prior to sentencing,
sentences.zh: 在判刑前，

sentences.en: Sarah Graves' mother,
sentences.zh: 莎拉·格雷夫斯的母亲，

sentences.en: Mary, wrote to the court asking for leniency, saying that she didn't raise her daughter to be a raciSt.
sentences.zh: 玛丽（Mary），写信给法庭请求宽大处理，称她并没有把女儿培养成种族主义者。

sentences.en: Unbeknown to Mary,
sentences.zh: 玛丽不知道的是，

sentences.en: Sarah had already written to the court to say that her racist views had formed during her childhood, as her mother frequently used hateful racist language at home.
sentences.zh: 莎拉早已写信给法庭，称她的种族主义观点是在童年时期形成的，因为她的母亲在家里经常使用充满仇恨的种族主义语言。

sentences.en: Mary was questioned in court about the content of her daughter's letter, but she remained in denial, insisting she raised her children right.
sentences.zh: 玛丽在法庭上被问及女儿信中的内容，但她仍然予以否认，坚称她把孩子们教得很好。

sentences.en: Judge Henry Wingate said that Graves couldn't make the excuse that she was in the wrong place at the wrong time, because she was in the place she wanted to be, being the person
sentences.zh: 亨利·温盖特（Henry Wingate）法官表示，格雷夫斯不能以自己在错误的时间出现在错误的地点为借口，因为她当时就在她想在的地方，做着她想做的人，

sentences.en: she wanted to be, but just didn't want to get caught.
sentences.zh: 只是不想被抓到而已。

sentences.en: Craig's sister,
sentences.zh: 克雷格的姐姐，

sentences.en: Barbara, addressed Graves and Richards, saying,
sentences.zh: 芭芭拉（Barbara），对格雷夫斯和理查兹说道：

sentences.en: You sat, watched, encouraged, and rallied around as my brother was beaten.
sentences.zh: “我弟弟被殴打时，你们坐在旁边，看着、鼓励着，并围观起哄。”

sentences.en: Your thirst for the blood of an innocent
sentences.zh: “你们对无辜非裔美国人鲜血的渴望，

sentences.en: African-American caused you to pour more fuel on the fire.
sentences.zh: 让你们火上浇油。”

sentences.en: Craig's husband,
sentences.zh: 克雷格的丈夫，

sentences.en: James, who had mostly stayed silent during the court proceedings, told the young women.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯（James），在庭审期间大多保持沉默，他告诉这些年轻女性：

sentences.en: You texted everyone that night, but you couldn't call 911.
sentences.zh: “那天晚上你们给所有人发了短信，却没能拨打911。”

sentences.en: You were as much to blame as if you'd been behind the wheel.
sentences.zh: “你们的罪责和坐在驾驶座上的人一样重。”

sentences.en: You're babies yourselves, but I don't feel sorry for you.
sentences.zh: “你们自己还是孩子，但我一点也不可怜你们。”

sentences.en: You knew what you were doing.
sentences.zh: “你们知道自己在做什么。”

sentences.en: Shelby Richards was sentenced to eight years and Sarah Graves would serve five.
sentences.zh: 谢尔比·理查兹被判处八年监禁，莎拉·格雷夫斯服刑五年。

sentences.en: Speaking outside of court,
sentences.zh: 在庭外接受采访时，

sentences.en: Graves' mother,
sentences.zh: 格雷夫斯的母亲，

sentences.en: Mary, said she believed that presiding judge
sentences.zh: 玛丽表示，她认为主审法官

sentences.zh: 亨利·温盖特是种族主义者，应该被撤职。

sentences.en: Graves' attorney agreed, saying,
sentences.zh: 格雷夫斯的律师表示赞同，他说：

sentences.en: I was dealing with a black judge who was showing racial hatred towards white defendants.
sentences.zh: “我面对的是一位对白人被告表现出种族仇恨的黑人法官。”

sentences.en: He was being a raciSt.
sentences.zh: “他是个种族主义者。”

sentences.en: Everybody's raciSt.
sentences.zh: “每个人都是种族主义者。”

sentences.en: I'm convinced of that.
sentences.zh: “我对此深信不疑。”

sentences.en: Sometimes they know it.
sentences.zh: “有时他们知道自己是。”

sentences.en: Sometimes they don't know it.
sentences.zh: “有时他们自己都不知道。”

sentences.en: In response,
sentences.zh: 作为回应，

sentences.zh: 温盖特法官对《纽约时报》评论道，引用如下：

sentences.en: This notion of reverse discrimination is one that has plagued racial progress.
sentences.zh: “这种反向歧视的概念一直困扰着种族进步。”

sentences.en: The term usually signifies apathy for the rights bestowed upon African Americans, rights already enjoyed by most whites.
sentences.zh: “这个词通常意味着对非裔美国人所享有的权利漠不关心，而这些权利大多数白人早已享有。”

sentences.en: During
sentences.zh: 在

sentences.zh: 约翰·布拉拉克的量刑听证会上，

sentences.en: Pastor Brian Richardson testified on his behalf, telling the court that Blalack lacked a great deal of self-esteem and wanted to fit in.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩·理查森（Brian Richardson）牧师为他作证，告诉法庭布拉拉克缺乏自信，只想融入群体。

sentences.en: Pastor Richardson claimed that Blalack had been bullied by the group and had only joined them in order to survive, adding that at least three teens had taken their own lives
sentences.zh: 理查森牧师声称布拉拉克曾受到该团伙的欺凌，加入他们只是为了生存，并补充说至少有三名青少年在受到该团伙欺凌后自杀。

sentences.en: after being bullied by the group.
sentences.zh: “在受到该团伙欺凌后。”

sentences.en: Blalack read a statement directed at
sentences.zh: 布拉拉克宣读了一份针对

sentences.en: Craig Anderson's family, saying that he wanted to make amends in any way he could and asked for their forgiveness.
sentences.zh: 克雷格·安德森家人的声明，称他想尽一切可能弥补过错，并请求他们的原谅。

sentences.en: Judge Wingate wasn't convinced that Blalack had shown any real remorse and fully expected that he'd align himself with racist groups once in prison.
sentences.zh: 温盖特法官并不相信布拉拉克表现出了任何真正的悔意，并完全预期他一旦入狱就会与种族主义团体为伍。

sentences.en: He urged
sentences.zh: 他敦促

sentences.en: Blalack to prove his sincerity by rebuilding his character before sentencing him to
sentences.zh: 布拉拉克在被判处

sentences.zh: 八天后，

sentences.zh: 罗伯特·赖斯，虽然在克雷格遇害当晚不在现场，但参与了其他袭击，被判处10年监禁。

sentences.zh: 约翰·赖斯、
